name: Lingwulong
isnote: Xu and colleagues (2018) described it as a diplodocoid (flagellicaudatan), while Mannion and Moore (2025) recovered it as sister of Cetiosauriscus, either outside Flagellicaudata or inside Diplodocidae; Diplodocoidea is used as the clade closest to both.
sum: Lingwulong is a Middle Jurassic sauropod from Ningxia, China, once seen as the oldest known diplodocoid and earliest neosauropod.
wsnote: No body-length estimate was read in the sources consulted.
holotype: LM V001a, the rear of a skull with dentary teeth in their original positions; the paratype and holotype may belong to one individual.
material: Remains of seven to ten individuals of different ages from quarries at Ciyaopu near Lingwu, covering nearly the whole skeleton.
biology: It had a U-shaped snout, unlike the square snout of most diplodocoids, and an ornamented upper margin of the orbit.
author: Xu et al. 2018
